title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning People's Tribunals
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the People's Tribunals

Fa Fa [1999] No. 20

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court at its 1067th meeting on June 10, 1999)

Article 1 These Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws, and in light of the work experience and actual circumstances of people's tribunals, for the purpose of strengthening the construction of people's tribunals and giving full play to their functions and roles.

Article 2 For the convenience of parties in instituting actions and of people's courts in adjudicating cases, a basic people's court may, as needed, establish people's tribunals.

Article 3 People's tribunals shall be established in light of such factors as the size of the area, the population, the number of cases, and the state of economic development, and shall not be subject to administrative divisions.

Article 4 A people's tribunal is a dispatched institution and a component part of the basic people's court, and shall work under the leadership of the basic people's court. Any judgment or ruling made by a people's tribunal shall be deemed as a judgment or ruling of the basic people's court.

Article 5 The higher people's court shall provide guidance and supervision over the work of people's tribunals.

Article 6 The tasks of a people's tribunal are:
(1) To hear civil cases and criminal cases that are prosecuted privately; where conditions permit, to hear economic cases;
(2) To handle enforcement matters in cases adjudicated by the tribunal;
(3) To guide the work of the people's mediation committees;
(4) To handle other matters assigned by the basic people's court.

Article 7 A people's tribunal shall adjudicate cases independently according to law, and shall not be subject to interference by any administrative organ, social organization, or individual.

Article 8 A people's tribunal shall hear cases in public, except those that are not to be heard in public according to law; for cases not heard in public, the judgment shall still be pronounced publicly.

Article 9 The following conditions must be satisfied for the establishment of a people's tribunal:
(1) There shall be at least three judges and one clerk; where conditions permit, judicial police may be assigned;
(2) There shall be a trial court and necessary ancillary facilities;
(3) There shall be office premises, office equipment, communication facilities, and means of transportation;
(4) Other conditions as required.

Article 10 The establishment or dissolution of a people's tribunal shall be reported by the basic people's court level by level to the higher people's court for approval.

Article 11 The name of a people's tribunal shall be determined by the place where it is located, and shall be prefixed with the name of the basic people's court to which it belongs.

Article 12 Judges of a people's tribunal must meet the conditions prescribed in the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China, and shall be appointed and removed in accordance with the procedures provided by law.
Judges of a people's tribunal may not concurrently hold positions in other state organs, enterprises, or institutions.

Article 13 A people's tribunal shall have a presiding judge, and may have a deputy presiding judge as needed.
The presiding judge and deputy presiding judge of a people's tribunal shall have at least three years of trial work experience.
The presiding judge and deputy presiding judge of a people's tribunal shall have the same rank as the presiding judges and deputy presiding judges of the trial divisions of the same court. The presiding judge of a people's tribunal shall be rotated on a regular basis.

Article 14 In addition to adjudicating cases, the presiding judge of a people's tribunal shall have the following duties:
(1) To preside over the daily work of the people's tribunal;
(2) To convene tribunal meetings;
(3) To decide on the acceptance of cases, determine the applicable trial procedure, and designate the composition of the collegial panel and the sole judge;
(4) To be responsible for the administrative management of the tribunal's personnel, performance assessment, and recommending rewards and disciplinary actions.
The deputy presiding judge shall assist the presiding judge in his/her work. When the presiding judge is unable to perform his/her duties for any reason, the deputy presiding judge shall act on his/her behalf.

Article 15 When a people's tribunal hears a case, a clerk must be present to make a record; the judge hearing the case shall not make the record himself/herself.

Article 16 When a collegial panel cannot be formed for the trial of a case by a people's tribunal due to the withdrawal of a judge or other circumstances, the president of the court shall designate another judge of the same court to hear the case.

Article 17 When a people's tribunal hears a case, it may form a collegial panel composed of judges and people's assessors. People's assessors, when performing their duties, have the same rights and obligations as judges.

Article 18 As needed, a people's tribunal may conduct circuit trials and hear cases on the spot.

Article 19 Where a people's tribunal takes compulsory measures against a participant in the proceedings or any other person who obstructs the proceedings, such as summoning by force, imposing a fine, or detention, it must report to the president of the court for approval.

Article 20 Where the opinions of the collegial panel are inconsistent or the presiding judge deems it necessary when a people's tribunal hears a case, the case may be reported to the president of the court for submission to the judicial committee for discussion and decision.

Article 21 Litigation documents such as judgments, rulings, mediation agreements, decisions, and summonses by force made by a people's tribunal shall be affixed with the seal of the people's court to which it belongs.

Article 22 A people's tribunal shall guide mediators in mediating disputes and help them summarize experience in mediating civil disputes among the people.

Article 23 Where a people's tribunal finds that an agreement reached by a people's mediation committee in mediating a civil dispute violates the law, it shall correct such violation.

Article 24 A people's tribunal may participate in comprehensive management of public security through adjudicating cases, carrying out legal education and publicity, and making judicial suggestions.

Article 25 A people's tribunal shall not participate in administrative law enforcement activities.

Article 26 A people's tribunal shall establish and improve working and management systems, including case registration, statistics, archive management, litigation fee management, and personnel attendance and performance assessment.

Article 27 Judges of a people's tribunal shall serve the people wholeheartedly, adhere to the work style of seeking truth from facts and the mass line, listen to the opinions of the masses, and accept the supervision of the masses.

Article 28 Judges of a people's tribunal shall handle cases impartially according to law and abide by trial discipline. They shall not accept invitations or gifts from parties or their agents, nor engage in embezzlement, bribery, favoritism, or perversion of the law in rendering judgments.

Article 29 The higher people's courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in accordance with these Provisions and in light of local actual circumstances, formulate implementation measures and report them to the Supreme People's Court for the record.

Article 30 These Provisions shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

July 15, 1999
